newsitem.title: ANGOLA: IMF head urges reconstruction of Angolan economy.
newsitem.headline: IMF head urges reconstruction of Angolan economy.

text.p: International Monetary Fund (IMF) managing director Michel Camdessus has urged the Angolan government and rebel Unita movement to jointly set a post-war reconstruction programme to restore confidence in the economy.

"We hope that from the moment a unity government is installed it should begin finding the key elements of a programme of reconstruction based on stability and reforms," Camdessus told a joint ceasefire commission meeting on Monday night at the start of a three-day visit to Angola.
The commission, including the government, Unita and the United Nations, is overseeing implementation of a 1994 peace accord to end two decades of civil war.
Last year the IMF withdrew its representative from the oil and mineral-rich country after the government failed to implement real economic reforms for the fourth time since 1987.

The IMF has been invited back by a new government recently reshuffled by President Jose Eduardo dos Santos, who called for economic reform. The new government is keen for IMF support to boost investor confidence and has pleaded for treatment as a "special case".
The country faces the massive task of not only rebuilding infrastructure but also getting funding to reintegrate about 100,000 government and Unita troops who are about to be demobilised.
The economic situation has become a direct threat to the demobilisation programme, with many foreign donors making aid dependent on better economic management.

The new government has taken emergency measures to stabilise the currency and reorganise financial structures, particularly the national bank. It cut monthly inflation to 38 percent in July from 61 percent in June and introduced a single exchange rate.

It also introduced a 50 percent subsidy on the price of bread, controlled profit margins and has tried to regulate commercial behaviour, particularly the speculative use of foreign exchange in import-export transactions.
"We are trying to see if the steps that the government has taken establishes a quality programme for the country," Camdessus said.
He said the IMF would work with the World Bank and other international organisations to help Angola.

"I have held meetings with the government and the economic team aimed at seeing how to establish the best possible programme to spare the Angolan people additional suffering...how to help them create the conditions for improvement and the strengthening of economic structures which will enable the country to make up for lost time."

He said Angola not only had to rebuild its economy, but also needed to integrate itself into the world economy. He said the international community was waiting to give a signal of approval: "We hope this day will be very soon."
Economists in Luanda said the IMF would particularly look at government efforts to make its oil account more transparent, cut inflation and control the budget deficit.
